question.text: A fund generated annual returns of 8%, 12%, and -3% over three consecutive years. What is the difference between the Arithmetic Mean Return (AMR) and Geometric Mean Return (GMR)?

explanation.text: The Logic: AMR = (8% + 12% + (-3%)) / 3 = 17% / 3 = 5.67%. GMR = [(1.08)(1.12)(0.97)]^(1/3) - 1 = [1.173312]^(1/3) - 1 = 1.05471 - 1 = 5.47% (rounded). Difference = 5.67% - 5.47% = 0.20 percentage point. Per NISM Series X-A pages 271-272, GMR is always less than or equal to AMR, with equality only when all yearly returns are identical. The Trap: Option C reverses AMR and GMR — GMR is ALWAYS less than or equal to AMR. Option A claims they are equal, which only happens when there is zero variance in returns. Option D uses an incorrect AMR calculation. Note: Use GMR for reporting long-term compounded performance; AMR overstates returns when there is variability across periods.
